deities: Saptashrungi Devi (presiding deity; 18-armed Mahishasura Mardini form of Goddess Durga/Parvati, swayambhu idol emerging from the rock face)
festivals: Chaitrotsav / Chaitra Navratri (Ram Navami to Chaitra Purnima; the year's biggest gathering - up to a million devotees on the final days)

history.dynasty: Ancient/puranic tradition (no historical dynasty attested); steps attributed to Umabai Dabhade, 1710
history.summary: The Saptashrungi Devi Mandir crowns the Saptashrungi hill - the 'Goddess of the Seven Peaks' - near Nanduri village, Kalvan taluka, Nashik district, about 60-65 km from Nashik city. It is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas (tradition holds that Sati's right arm fell here) and one of Maharashtra's three-and-a-half Shakti Peethas, alongside Mahalakshmi (Kolhapur), Bhavani (Tuljapur) and Renuka (Mahur). The presiding deity is the 18-armed Mahishasura Mardini, said to have vanquished the buffalo demon here; the idol is swayambhu, carved from the natural rock, and leans slightly left - legend links this to Sage Markandeya, who is said to have recited the 700 verses of the Devi Mahatmya (Durga Saptashati) before her here. Hanuman is believed to have visited these hills seeking medicinal herbs for Lakshmana. The 500-odd steps to the shrine are attributed to Umabai Dabhade (1710), and a ropeway/funicular trolley was added in 2018; devotees also climb barefoot during Chaitra Purnima.

name: Saptashrungi Devi Mandir
town: Vani (CSV town 'Nashik' is approximate - the temple is at Saptashrungi Gad near Nanduri village, Kalvan taluka, about 60-65 km from Nashik city)
town_description: Vani is a small village in Dindori taluka of Nashik district, Maharashtra, serving as the base for the Saptashrungi hill pilgrimage. The area around Vani and Nanduri lies in the Sahyadri ranges, with the temple perched at about 1,230 m elevation on a hill of seven peaks. During Chaitra and Ashwin Navratri the quiet village road turns into a pilgrimage corridor of devotees, MSRTC buses and dharamshalas.

travel.airport: Nashik (Ozar) Airport (approx. 53 km; verify); Mumbai International Airport about 230-250 km
travel.railway: Nashik Road Railway Station (approx. 65-70 km; verify)
travel.road: About 60-65 km from Nashik city; MSRTC buses run from Nashik Central Bus Stand to Vani/Nanduri, then shared autos or temple shuttles to the base; a ropeway and about 510 steps cover the final ascent.

visitor_information.best_time: October-March for clear hill weather; Chaitra Navratri and Ashwin Navratri are the grand festival periods.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): commonly listed as 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM daily; some sources list 5:00 AM to 9:00/10:00 PM, with extended hours during festivals.
